source: Gugerty & Olson (1986) Debugging by skilled and novice programmers (CHI 86)
finding: Full text not obtained. ACM DL and Taylor & Francis returned 403, Academia and Bohrium were blocked or showed only a bot wall. Gap 1 stays open.
numbers: No sample sizes, times, accuracy or bug-addition counts could be verified. Secondary sources say two experiments, Pascal and LOGO programs, and a Pascal-like LOGO subset all subjects knew.
limits: Secondary summaries only; the 18/6/3/1 snippet figures stay unverified.
agent_relevance: Do not cite effect sizes for 'novices add bugs' from this paper. Treat it as a qualitative design prior.

source: Kinnunen (2007) MSc thesis, section 2.1 restating G&O 1986
finding: Restates the G&O cycle: read description and code, form a hypothesis, test it by editing, running or checking the description, and go back if no bug is found. Says neither novices nor experts debugged randomly.
numbers: No numbers given. Novices 'seldom found the bugs in the first try' and 'added new bugs'; same cycle as experts but slower.
quote: novice and expert programmers did not act any different but novices needed more time
limits: Second-hand and shows no counts. It adds nothing quantitative beyond a08.
agent_relevance: The loop 'hypothesis, test, fall back to the spec' is the same loop an agent runs. The difference is quality of the first hypothesis, not the loop.

source: Katz & Anderson (1987) Debugging: An analysis of bug-location strategies. Human-Computer Interaction 3(4)
finding: Full text and abstract not obtained (Taylor & Francis 403; the ACT-R publication mirror did not respond). DOI confirmed through Crossref. Gap 6 stays open.
numbers: None verified.
limits: Metadata only.
agent_relevance: Cannot say whether forward or backward bug-location differs in success. Do not build a rule on it.

source: Tsui (2025) Self-Correction Bench: the Self-Correction Blind Spot in LLMs
finding: The same injected error is fixed far less often when the model sees it as its own output than when it is attributed to the user. The capability exists but is not used.
numbers: 14 open-source non-reasoning models: average blind spot 64.5%. Closed models: Claude 3.5 Haiku 52.5%, Sonnet 4 41.4%. Non-math (BIG-Bench Mistake logic and tracking) average 62.8%. Fine-tuning on 5,306 correction traces cuts it 76.0%. Appending 'Wait' cuts it 89.3%.
quote: models correct external errors but fail on identical internal ones
limits: Injected errors, not natural ones; reasoning tasks mostly math; the on-policy check is a smaller sample.
agent_relevance: Own-output errors are the ones an agent will miss. Frame the fix pass as a review of someone else's work, and use a short cue like 'Wait' before revision.

source: Tsui (2025) Self-Correction Bench, section 4.4 reasoning models
finding: Reasoning models show a small or negative blind spot. Appending 'Wait' to a non-reasoning base model nearly closes the gap to its reasoning sibling.
limits: Same benchmark of injected errors; says nothing about open-ended edits or repo-level bugs.
agent_relevance: Partly answers gap 9: reasoning models do notice own errors inside their own chain. The Huang harm may shrink for them on the same task, but see d06.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) Understanding the Dark Side of LLMs' Intrinsic Self-Correction
finding: Intrinsic self-correction with no outside signal still flips correct answers on reasoning-tuned models of late 2024, though less than on older chat models.
numbers: Yes/No QA, ChatGPT o1-mini: accuracy 62.5 after revision, a drop of 12.1 points, 34.0% of initially correct answers overturned. o1-preview: 74.1, drop 4.2, 15.6% overturned. Llama-3.1-8B worst: drop 20.4 points, 58.8% overturned. Models tested: o1, 4o, 3.5-turbo, Llama 2/3/3.1, DeepSeek V3/R1.
limits: Programming table columns are garbled in the PDF text, so code numbers were not used. HumanEval has 161 functions. No 2026 models.
agent_relevance: Gap 9 is answered only for o1-class models of late 2024: harm persists. No data on 2026 models. Keep the 'revise only on an external signal' guardrail.

source: Ehrlich et al. (2025) CodeMonkeys: Scaling Test-Time Compute for Software Engineering
finding: A cheap model reads every file once per issue, flags relevant ones, and a ranking step trims context. Reading everything is affordable when the cost is shared across many edits.
numbers: Scan averages 2.94M tokens per problem and is under 15% of total cost. Context kept averages 74,570 tokens, a 50.5x cut. At a 128k limit, 92.6% of instances have all needed files in context.
limits: Reading was done by a small model, then compressed. It is not a test of capped reading against full reading at equal tokens. Gap 2 stays open.
agent_relevance: Broad cheap read, then rank down to a short context, matches the 'expert reads less' pattern in effect while the read itself is not skipped.

source: Ehrlich et al. (2025) CodeMonkeys, serial versus parallel compute
finding: At equal inference cost, many short state machines and few long ones reach similar coverage. Extra iterations do not rescue a run that already approved its own wrong work; a new sample is a fresh start.
numbers: Coverage (any candidate correct) 69.8% on SWE-bench Verified with 10 state machines x 8 iterations. Authors state the frontier is flat across serial/parallel splits after the first few.
quote: Increasing the iteration limit further does not help "stuck" state machines
limits: Not a test of 'restart after 2 failed rounds' with a reasoning model. Different design from Adnan and Kuhn.
agent_relevance: Supports capping edits per round and starting fresh instead of grinding. It is indirect support for K10, not a replication.

source: Ehrlich et al. (2025) CodeMonkeys, selection
finding: Keeping the best candidate matters a lot: choosing well is worth more than generating more.
numbers: Oracle selection 69.8%; random selection 45.8%; their method 57.4% at about 2300 USD. Ensemble selection over existing top submissions 66.2%, above the best member.
limits: Selection used model-written tests plus a final selection run; not the same as keep-best-so-far across rounds.
agent_relevance: Keep-best-so-far has a large possible gain (11.6 points between random and method; 12.4 more to oracle) if the selector is good.

source: Meng et al. (2025) LLM-based Agents for Automated Bug Fixing: How Far Are We?
finding: Across six repair systems on SWE-bench Verified, ranking by file-level localization F1 matches ranking by issue resolution (one exception). Localization is where systems differ.
numbers: 500 tasks. Best system W&B Programmer 255 resolved (51%); it localized at least one buggy file in 448 cases and all buggy files in 394. Lowest system localized 342 (31.0% gap). Symbol level: 396 vs 308 (28.6%).
limits: Localization read off the final patch, not from the trace. Correlation across six systems, not a causal test.
agent_relevance: Backs K08. Diagnosis quality is the best predictor of final fix. Partly answers gap 8 at system level, not per trace.

source: Wang, Pradel & Liu (2026) Are 'Solved Issues' in SWE-bench Really Solved Correctly? (ICSE 26)
finding: Test-passing patches are often wrong. Differential testing finds behaviour changes the tests miss.
numbers: Three tools (CodeStory, LearnByInteract, OpenHands) on SWE-bench Verified: 7.8% of plausible patches fail the full developer tests; 29.6% (260 of 877) behave differently from the gold patch; 28.6% of divergent ones certainly incorrect; reported rates inflated by 6.4 points.
limits: Only three tools, Python repos. 46.8% of divergences are different-but-similar implementations, 27.3% do more than the gold patch.
agent_relevance: Evidence for gap 3 at patch level: agents add unwanted behaviour. A rise in regression checks per edit is justified.

source: Wang, Pradel & Liu (2026) incorrect-patch categories
finding: Among 22 manually confirmed incorrect plausible patches, half broke existing behaviour. This is the closest LLM match to 'novices add bugs'.
numbers: Regressive Patches 11 of 22 (50.0%); 8 of 22 (36.4%) from faulty supplementary changes; 11 of 22 (50.0%) were not caught by running all developer tests.
limits: Small sample of 22. A rate per edit was not measured, only per accepted patch. Gap 3 (per-edit new failing tests, effect of an edit cap) stays open.
agent_relevance: Require a pass-to-pass regression run before keeping an edit, and discourage supplementary changes.

source: Liu et al. (2025) An Empirical Study on Failures in Automated Issue Solving
finding: Manual analysis of 150 failed instances gives a taxonomy of 3 phases, 9 categories, 25 subcategories. Pipeline tools fail at localization; agents fail by looping on a failed strategy.
numbers: SWE-bench Verified 500 tasks: OpenHands 53.0% (265), Agentless 50.8% (254), Tools Claude 49.0% (245). Agentless: 51.3% of failures contain a localization error. Agents: 49.1% (OpenHands) and 51.7% (Tools Claude) contain an iteration/validation error. Flawed reasoning is the top root cause; knowledge deficiency about 25%; environment about 10%.
quote: the lack of an effective mechanism for self-correction
limits: Annotation by humans on one benchmark with 2024 tools. Root-cause shares are read from text and a figure.
agent_relevance: Matches the 'stay on a failed strategy' mode. Add a stall rule: after a failed round change the hypothesis, not just the patch.

source: Liu et al. (2025) Expert-Executor framework
finding: A second agent reviews the plan and the fix before writing code. It resolved some tasks the baseline had failed.
numbers: 24 of 108 previously failed OpenHands issues resolved (22.2%). Both agents use Claude 3.5 Sonnet; Expert is consulted at passive review intervals of 25 within 40 rounds.
limits: Same model in both roles, so this is not 'stronger diagnosis'. Run only on previously failed tasks, with no matched-token control seen in the text. Gap 5 stays open.
agent_relevance: Separate reviewer helps on stuck cases, but it is not yet shown to beat spending the same tokens on resampling (K09).

source: Zhong et al. (2024) Debug like a Human: LDB, runtime-state debugging
finding: Giving the model block-level runtime values to judge each basic block beats whole-program feedback.
numbers: HumanEval, GPT-3.5: no debugger 73.8, Self-Debug 81.1 (+7.3), LDB 82.9 (+9.1). Abstract: up to 9.8% gain over baselines on HumanEval, MBPP, TransCoder.
limits: Small benchmarks; column order read from the table. Not a reading-cap test.
agent_relevance: Diagnosis improves when it is anchored on observed state, which fits the expert behaviour of testing hypotheses against the program.

source: Antoniades et al. (2025) SWE-Search: MCTS and iterative refinement for software agents
finding: Tree search with backtracking and a value agent improves agents that otherwise run a single straight line.
numbers: 23% relative gain on average over the baseline across five models on SWE-bench; Qwen-2.5-72B with search exceeds GPT-4o in the original framework.
limits: Gain mixes search width and self-feedback; compute is higher than baseline.
agent_relevance: Evidence for branching with a keep-best rule over linear editing.

source: Wang et al. (2025) Thoughts Are All Over the Place: underthinking of o1-like LLMs
finding: Reasoning models switch thoughts too often on wrong answers. A penalty on switching raises accuracy with no training.
numbers: Abstract only read in detail; per-model counts in the PDF were garbled and were not used. Models: QwQ-32B-Preview, DeepSeek-R1-Preview on three hard test sets.
limits: Math focus, not debugging.
agent_relevance: The opposite failure to novices adding edits: too much hypothesis hopping. A schema should limit both.

source: Yu et al. (2025) UTBoost: rigorous evaluation of coding agents on SWE-Bench
finding: Written tests in SWE-bench are often too weak, so wrong patches count as solved.
numbers: Found 36 task instances with insufficient test cases and 345 erroneous patches wrongly accepted.
limits: Covers SWE-Bench Lite and Verified leaderboards at one point in time.
agent_relevance: Treat 'tests pass' as weak evidence for keep-best. Add extra checks.

source: Eye-tracking and modern cohorts search (Crossref, 2015-2026)
finding: Only titles seen: Spatial Temporal Eye-Tracking Indicators of Novice Programmers' Skill (IEEE Access 2026) and A Fine-grained Assessment on Novice Programmers' Gaze Patterns on Pseudocode Problems (ETRA 2020). No abstracts, no PDFs opened.
numbers: None.
limits: No replication of 'experts form hypotheses from less code' was found or read. Gap 7 stays open.
agent_relevance: No claim.
